children: fell 9.93% intraday after announcing a proposed $1.0 billion offering of 0% convertible senior notes due September

2031, with a further $150 million available to underwriters to cover over-allotments. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, RBC Capital Markets and Citigroup are joint lead book-running managers.

The notes convert into Axon stock at a rate set at pricing, with Axon able to settle in cash, shares or both. Part of the proceeds buys capped call transactions covering the shares initially underlying the notes, limiting dilution up to a cap. The rest goes to general corporate purposes, which Axon says may include acquisitions or investments.

At the end of the second quarter, Axon held $685 million of cash, equivalents and short-term investments against $1.75 billion of notes, a net debt position of $1.1 billion. Revenue grew 35% to $904 million and adjusted EBITDA reached $242 million, but free cash flow was negative $1 million in the quarter and negative $55.6 million across six months. Receivables and contract assets absorbed $306 million and inventory $80 million.

title: Axon Stock Falls 10% on a $1 Billion Convertible Offering
